stations.name: What it covers
stations.meaning: Which hazard, which asset, which parts; what is left out
stations.paragraph: Flood on buildings: FEMA Hazus depth-damage functions used as published, one per building (house DF 129, warehouse DF 341, office DF 431, each for river and coastal still water); retail keeps Hazus DF 217 for river water and USACE NACCS for coastal surge. It names 4 parts: House, Warehouse, Office and Retail. Outside its scope: contents (declared as a withheld placeholder part) and land, site works, business interruption. Kinds of damage it does not include: waves and fast-moving water (wave and velocity zones).

stations.name: What breaks
stations.meaning: The parts of the plant the hazard damages, each with its own curve
stations.paragraph: For this hazard the building is split into 4 parts: House, Warehouse, Office and Retail. 1 further unit is named but withheld — fre building contents — a stated 'not zero', not a curve.

stations.name: How damage is measured
stations.meaning: The hazard intensity on the x-axis and the shape of the curve
stations.paragraph: Damage is read against water depth above the first floor (ft). The curve is a line through fixed points (piecewise linear). The input, in the catalogue's words: water depth above the first floor (ft), -4 to 24 ft (retail coastal curve -1 to 10 ft); depth above ground is accepted with the building's floor height.

stations.name: Where the numbers come from
stations.meaning: The sources, what was taken from each, and how sure we are
stations.paragraph: 13 sources set this cell: FEMA. Hazus Flood Model Technical Manual, Hazus 7.0 (June 2025), Table 5-2 Default Damage Functions for…, FEMA Hazus team. Hazus 6.1 flood damage-function extract, HazusFloodDamageFunctions_Hazus61.xlsx…, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (2015) and FEMA OpenFEMA NFIP redacted claims, v3 (FRE-S012; check only) and 9 more. Of the 20 parameters, 15 are lab-tested (T2), 3 are transferred (T3) and 2 are our judgment (T4). The source and claim registers are machine-readable files in the cell folder. 1 source has no link in the register (1 with a locator).

stations.name: What it is worth
stations.meaning: The share of the plant's value the curves cover
stations.paragraph: The damage ratio is a share of structure replacement cost new of the same building (no land, contents or depreciation). The files state no plant-level dollar figure for this asset.

stations.name: The audit
stations.meaning: The seven checks a curve passes before release
stations.paragraph: The seven-step audit is a file in the cell folder with 7 rows; the statuses it records: partial and proposed. A site-condition adapter has not been written for this cell.

stations.name: The files
stations.meaning: The runtime file, the write-up and the workbook
stations.paragraph: The runtime file is the curve artifact with 7 curve records (model v0.2, docs r1). The write-up is flood_real_estate_curve_derivation_dossier__model_v0_2__docs_r1.md. The workbook is damage_curve_records_flood_real_estate__model_v0_2__docs_r1.xlsx. The cell folder holds 41 files, each with its SHA under Details.

stations.name: What it can output
stations.meaning: What a consumer may compute with this curve
stations.paragraph: One flood event is available only under conditions the consumer (Hazard) checks. A dollar scenario, yearly loss and PML and VaR are not supported. Annual metrics belong to the consumer; nothing here is an expected annual loss.

stations.name: How it was tested
stations.meaning: The known answers this build reproduced
stations.paragraph: This build reproduced 185 of 185 known answers through the cell's evaluator (within 1e-12 on the damage ratio). 5 were not run: prose assertions; not executable. The validation record says report. 1 outside check: NFIP flood-insurance claims by depth band (about 105,000 claims).

stations.name: Seen in the field, and reviewed
stations.meaning: Field reports of this damage, and who has read the entry
stations.paragraph: Not searched — nobody has looked for field reports yet. The catalogue entry has been read by an agent only (2026-10-19); no person has reviewed it yet. The curve release carries its own review state: not yet reviewed.

claims.text: Wave impact, fast-moving water and scour are a separate mechanism from still-water inundation: they act by force and undermining, depend on wave height or flow speed rather than depth, and depend strongly on site exposure, foundation and soil. They are excluded from flood_inundation_contact and deferred, with wave damage withheld rather than set to zero.
claims.locator: flood_wind D-FW-07 and FW-C012 (scour, erosion, debris and wave loading excluded; foundation withheld not zero); flood_solar FS_FOUND (T4 velocity/scour placeholder); Hazus 7.0 section 5.4.1.1.2.1 (BCAR coastal curves assume waves of 1.5 ft or more destroy walls); NACCS 2015 publishes wave and erosion tables separately from inundation
claims.update_trigger: Hazard supplies wave height or flow speed, and wave or velocity curves are curated.

claims.text: NSI 2026 assigns first-floor height by foundation type; RES1 slab foundations default to 0.75 ft and basements to 2 ft, informed by a 2021 USACE survey and generally aligned with median survey values (the 2022 edition stated 0.5 ft for RES1 slab).
claims.locator: NSI 2026 Foundation Type and Height; NSI 2022 same section
claims.update_trigger: A later NSI edition changes it.

claims.text: In NSI records for three counties, slab-foundation COM1, COM4, COM2 and IND2 structures carry first-floor height 0.25 ft (91.5-100% of records) and slab RES1-1SNB structures carry 0.75 ft (100%).
claims.update_trigger: NSI documents non-residential defaults.

claims.text: NSI fullrep is replacement cost new (occupancy, floor area, occupancy-specific cost per area; national cost curve with local wage adjustment; RES1 also adjusted by tract income; August 2025 prices; cost per area falls with size). val_struct is depreciated 1% per year for 20 years, then held at 80%.
claims.locator: NSI 2026 Full Replacement Cost; field list

claims.text: Hazus rounds first-floor height above grade to the nearest whole foot (0.5 ft and below down, 0.51 ft and above up) when it applies its curves to user-defined facilities.
claims.update_trigger: Owner asks to reproduce Hazus exactly.

claims.text: The FEMA freshwater curves agree with NFIP claims within about 6 points for the house at 2-6 ft above the floor and for the commercial analogue at 0-10 ft; both curves sit below the claims at shallow depth.
claims.update_trigger: A rerun on a newer pull or a changed curve.

claims.text: The NACCS coastal house curve (5A) is 12-23 points below NFIP coastal-surge claims in the first 2 ft above the floor, where 72% of the compared coastal house claims fall; the claims sit near the NACCS upper bound.
claims.update_trigger: A rerun, or claims evidence from the North Atlantic.

claims.text: The NACCS coastal commercial curve (prototype 2) is 6-12 points above NFIP coastal-surge claims for the commercial analogue from 1 ft above the floor.
claims.update_trigger: A rerun, or an office-specific comparison.

claims.text: Applied to the same coastal-surge claims, the FEMA freshwater curves are 8-12 points below the house claims at 0-2 ft and within 7 points at 2-6 ft, and 7-10 points below the commercial claims at 0-6 ft.
claims.update_trigger: Owner coastal decision.

claims.text: NFIP coastal-surge claims match freshwater claims for the house analogue at the same depth (within 5 points at 0-6 ft), but run 2-11 points higher for the commercial analogue.
claims.update_trigger: A rerun or a salinity-specific study.

claims.text: The shallow-depth gap for the house is sensitive to the assumed first-floor height: for claims 0.5-2.0 ft above grade, the freshwater curve is 3 points below the claims at a 0 ft floor height and 10 points below at the reference 0.75 ft.
claims.update_trigger: Observed floor heights for the claims, or Hazard's grade-to-floor conversion.

claims.text: Hazus DF 431 (COM4, Average Prof/Tech Services, Structure, USACE Galveston) is identical at all 29 knots (-4 to 24 ft) in the Pollack compilation, USACE go-consequences and the Hazus 6.1 extract.
claims.locator: OFFICE_FLOOD_RESEARCH_flood_real_estate__model_v0_1__docs_r1.md §2; haz_fl_dept.csv DmgFnId 431 (flBldgStructDmgFn); occtypes.json COM4 structure; flBldgStrucDmgFn ID 431
claims.update_trigger: A newer Hazus release changes DF 431.

claims.text: FEMA's default structure curve for COM4 is DF 431 at every height class (under 4, 4-7, over 7 storeys), with or without basement, and for riverine, coastal A and coastal V hazards.
claims.locator: Hazus 6.1 flBldgStructDmgFinal rows C4LN, C4LB, C4MN, C4MB, C4HN, C4HB (HazardR, HazardCA, HazardCV = 1); SOoccupId_Occ_Xref
claims.update_trigger: A Hazus release with height-specific commercial defaults.

claims.text: In NFIP business claims (occupancy 4, 6, 18; slab), damage as a share of the building falls with the number of floors: at matched depth bands two floors show about 0.75 of the one-floor ratio (freshwater; 0.67 coastal) and three or more floors about 0.5 (freshwater, up to 3 ft).
claims.update_trigger: Office-specific or height-specific claims evidence.

claims.text: On the same NFIP business claims, DF 431 is within 1 point of one-floor freshwater claims and about 3.5 points (x1.6) above three-or-more-floor freshwater claims; in coastal surge it is within 2-5 points of two-floor and taller claims, while NACCS prototype 2 is 11-13 points above them.
claims.update_trigger: Owner office and coastal decisions.

claims.text: Other Hazus office structure curves do not fit better: DF 438 (Big Office Commercial) is within 2-3 points of DF 431 on the claims, DF 466 (Wilmington Office Building) is 21-34 points above every claims group, and the New Orleans office curves (DF 444-462) reach 65-100% by 3 ft.
claims.update_trigger: A height- or size-specific office curve is found.

claims.text: For the warehouse there is little coastal claims evidence: on 14 NFIP coastal-surge claims with a warehouse building description at 1-3 ft above the floor (mean damage 14%), Hazus DF 341 reads 7% and NACCS prototype 3 reads 26%; on all 1-floor business coastal claims DF 341 is 11-13 points below and NACCS prototype 3 1-13 points above.
claims.locator: NFIP pulls in build/nfip_claims (nonres.json); computed 2026-10-16 with the v0.1 records
claims.update_trigger: More coastal warehouse claims or a warehouse-specific coastal study.

parameters.name: axis_definition
parameters.value: flood depth above first finished floor, ft
parameters.reasoning: Native axis of both libraries (FRE-C001).
parameters.update_trigger: A source with a different reference elevation is adopted.

parameters.name: curve_form
parameters.value: straight lines between published points (piecewise linear)
parameters.reasoning: Reproduces every published value; smooth fits predict held-out points worse on all six point curves and move published values by 2-5 points (FORM_COMPARISON); table-based cells (flood_solar, flood_wind, wildfire_solar, wildfire_wind) use straight lines; method rule: simplest form the evidence yields.
parameters.update_trigger: A reviewed reason to prefer smoothness.

parameters.name: axis_bridge
parameters.value: depth_above_floor = depth_above_grade − first_floor_height (same datum required)
parameters.reasoning: Both libraries define depth relative to FFE; FFE = grade + first-floor height.
parameters.update_trigger: Hazard supplies depth on a different reference.

parameters.name: RE_RES_SFD_1S_SLAB.freshwater.ordinates
parameters.value: Hazus DF 129, −4 to 24 ft (USACE-IWR)
parameters.reasoning: FEMA Table 5-2 default; equals rounded USACE EGM means −2 to 16 ft (FRE-C002, C004).
parameters.update_trigger: NFIP claims comparison or a Hazus Table 5-2 change.

parameters.name: RE_COM_LOWRISE.freshwater.ordinates
parameters.value: Hazus DF 217, −4 to 24 ft (USACE Galveston, average of 47 retail classes)
parameters.reasoning: FEMA Table 5-2 default for COM1; verified identical to USACE copy (FRE-C003). Single-district provenance (FRE-C011).
parameters.update_trigger: Owner selects office (DF 431) or NFIP comparison shows bias.

parameters.name: RE_IND_WAREHOUSE.freshwater.ordinates
parameters.value: Hazus DF 341, −4 to 24 ft (USACE Galveston, average of 22 wholesale/warehouse classes)
parameters.reasoning: FEMA Table 5-2 default for COM2 (warehouse use); verified identical to USACE copy (FRE-C003). Single-district provenance.
parameters.update_trigger: Owner selects light industrial (DF 559) or NFIP comparison shows bias.

parameters.name: RE_COM_LOWRISE.coastal.ordinates
parameters.value: NACCS COM-ENG Min/ML/Max at the ten published depths
parameters.reasoning: Prototype 2 steel-framed commercial matches the reference building (FRE-C008). T3 transfer outside the North Atlantic.

parameters.name: RE_IND_WAREHOUSE.coastal.ordinates

parameters.name: naccs_runtime_band
parameters.value: ML is the point curve; Min and Max are building-variant bounds, not a probability spread
parameters.reasoning: NACCS defines Min/Max by building characteristics, not by probability.

parameters.name: naccs_knot_set
parameters.value: published depths only: −1, −0.5, 0, 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 10 ft
parameters.reasoning: Compiled values at 4, 6, 8, 9 ft are fills (FRE-C006, D-FRE-13).

parameters.name: valid_range.hazus
parameters.value: −4 to 24 ft; below −4 ft = 0%; above 24 ft withholds
parameters.reasoning: Published library range; every record is 0% at −4 ft; no extrapolation or clamp above (D-FRE-21, flood_wind precedent).

parameters.name: valid_range.naccs
parameters.value: −1 to 10 ft; below −1 ft = 0%; above 10 ft withholds
parameters.reasoning: Published report range; every NACCS curve is 0% at −1 ft; no extrapolation or clamp above (D-FRE-21).

parameters.name: water_type_conditioner
parameters.value: freshwater -> Hazus; coastal_surge_saline -> NACCS; unknown -> withhold
parameters.reasoning: Libraries built for different water and settings; FEMA's own coastal position recorded as alternative (FRE-C013).
parameters.update_trigger: Owner selects FEMA coastal defaults, or Hazard cannot supply water type.
